title: Development of Communication
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 5 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Play a game: send a message across the field by drum, by runner and by phone, and time each.

skills.key_step: The child names early forms of communication (drums, horns, smoke, whistles, ululation, messengers) and says how they carried news.

floor.question: How did people carry goods long ago?
floor.answer: on their heads, backs or by animals

representations: a message race on the field
steps: Say how far and how fast.
contexts: a horn calling elders to a meeting

board.say: How did smoke carry a message?

board.do: Wait for "people saw it from far".

misconceptions.ask: Which was an early form of communication in Kenya?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what was used before electricity.

misconceptions.ask: Why is a mobile phone faster than a messenger on foot?
misconceptions.repair: Time a runner and a phone call across the same distance.

misconceptions.ask: How did some communities use drums besides music?
misconceptions.repair: Beat two patterns: one for "come" and one for "danger".

misconceptions.ask: When could smoke signals be seen best?
misconceptions.repair: Ask whether you can see grey smoke in the dark.

checks.question: Give two early forms of communication.
checks.answer: any two of: drums, horns, smoke signals, whistles, ululation, messengers

checks.question: Was a messenger faster or slower than a phone call?

skills.key_step: The child names modern means of communication, picks the right one for a job and knows not everything online is true or safe.

floor.question: Name one early form of communication.

steps: Ask: sound, picture, words or a parcel?
contexts: the post office sending a parcel

board.do: Write: "tell farmers in many villages about a coming drought".

board.say: Which means reaches the most people?

misconceptions.ask: Which means of communication shows pictures and sound together?
misconceptions.repair: Describe what you can see and hear on each in a one-line list.

misconceptions.ask: You get a message that claims something shocking. What should you do first?
misconceptions.repair: Practise with a made-up rumour and ask who could check it.

listen_for: It is not; everyone has internet
misconceptions.ask: Why is radio still important in Kenya?
misconceptions.repair: Ask how a herder far from town hears the news.

misconceptions.ask: Someone you do not know asks for your address on a phone app. What do you do?
misconceptions.repair: Practise saying no and telling an adult.

checks.question: Which means would you use to send a parcel to an aunt in Kisumu?
checks.answer: the post office or a courier

checks.question: A message on the phone says you have won money and asks for your PIN. What should you do?
checks.answer: Do not reply and tell a parent
